name: Idiomatic Expression Analysis
description: Evaluates the frequency, accuracy, and contextual naturalness of idioms and colloquialisms. AI models tend to avoid culturally localized phraseology, and when forced to use it, often deploy popular idioms in clunky or highly literal ways.
algorithm: Non-Literal Lexical Density & Cultural Phrasing Detection
mechanism: Idioms ('bite the bullet', 'kick the bucket', 'under the weather') are linguistic anomalies. They are deeply tied to specific cultures, completely defy literal translation, and rely heavily on shared, unspoken contextual understanding between the writer and reader. Because LLMs are trained to maximize global accessibility and clarity to function as helpful assistants, their core probability distributions actively suppress highly localized, non-literal idioms that might confuse international users. When an AI is explicitly prompted to 'write casually' or 'use slang', it usually reaches for the most statistically common, clichéd idioms and inserts them abruptly, without the subtle syntactical blending a human would use. This algorithm matches text against a massive dictionary of thousands of language-specific idioms, phrasal verbs, and colloquialisms. It measures the 'Idiomatic Density' of the text. A complete absence of idiomatic language in what should be a casual human text, or the presence of awkwardly shoehorned, highly predictable idioms, flags the content as mathematically synthesized.
useCase: Essential for evaluating creative writing, personal blog posts, informal emails, marketing copy, and literature, where human authors naturally employ rich metaphorical language.
strengths:
• Highly effective on casual text; human colloquial writing is inherently messy and idiom-rich, while AI defaults to sterile, universally understood phrasing.
• Catches 'Idiom Hallucination'—where an AI model invents a phrase that sounds like an idiom but doesn't actually exist in the target culture.
• Resistant to simple synonym replacement, as replacing a word in an idiom usually destroys its meaning.
limitations:
• Completely irrelevant for formal academic papers, legal contracts, or technical documentation, where human style guides also demand the strict eradication of idiomatic language.
• Highly dependent on maintaining constantly updated, culturally specific idiom dictionaries for every supported language and regional dialect (e.g., US vs. UK English).
• Can misflag writing by non-native human speakers who are actively avoiding idioms to ensure they are understood.
parameters:
Analysis: N-gram Matching against Cultural Idiom Lexicons
Metric: Ratio of Non-Literal Idiomatic Phrasing vs Standard Literal Output
Output: 0-100 Idiomatic Sterility (Cultural Detachment) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-85% in informal, creative, or persuasive texts. Serves as a strong cultural fingerprinting tool that exposes an AI's globally standardized neutrality.

references.title: Jurafsky, D. & Martin, J.H. (2024). Speech and Language Processing. 3rd Edition.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
